capabilities: fetch all QEMU VMs and LXC containers from every node in a Proxmox cluster via one command
generate a Markdown table with VMID, name, status, resources, disks, OS and notes
authenticate with an API token or username plus password, including a test connection check
work with self-signed certificates by making TLS verification optional
configure destination folder and note name that regenerate on each update
extras: Desktop-only: it uses Node's https module directly to tolerate Proxmox's self-signed certificates. Credentials are stored in plain text in the plugin's data.json; the README advises a read-only PVEAuditor token and excluding that file from sync or version control. Not yet in the community catalog, so it must be installed manually or via BRAT.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to pull a live inventory of VMs and containers from a Proxmox server into a note.
summary: Proxmox VE integration that fetches virtual machines and LXC containers from a host or cluster and writes them into a Markdown inventory table.
